W2 (empirical), after E013. Best remains E010: 6.639 s, 0.7548 (8.5 ep, Muon+EMA+prog-res 24/28/32, last width 512). The margin over the 0.753 bar is 0.17 pp.

Measured (3 seeds, all complete): E001 9ep eager 0.7430/9.43. E004 compiled 0.7486/9.04. E005 +EMA 0.7583/9.10. E006 +Muon 0.7649/9.45. E007 +prog-res 0.7590/7.33. E008 8.5ep 0.7572/6.98. E009 LR floor 0 0.7564/6.99. E010 width 512 0.7548/6.64. E011 aggressive res 0.7451/5.70. E012 exact rerun of E010: bit-identical accuracy, time within 0.1%. E013 LS 0.2: 0.7551/6.630, i.e. +0.04 pp, which is noise.

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: -0.5 epoch costs about 0.18 pp and saves about 4.8% time. Roughly linear (E007 to E008).
2. Compile saved about 4% once the stride recompile leak was fixed (E003 to E004).
3. EMA/Lookahead: +0.97 pp for +0.06 s (E004 to E005). This is the cheapest gain and was far above my forecast.
4. Muon: +0.66 pp for +0.35 s (E005 to E006).
5. Progressive resizing: -22% time for -0.59 pp. Time tracks pixel count.
6. Width 576 to 512: -4.8% time for -0.25 pp, about the epoch-dial exchange rate.
7. LR floor 0 on top of EMA: no gain (E009). EMA and a low final LR are redundant.
8. Resolution cliff (E011): -14% time for -1.4 pp, about 3x worse than the E007 rate.
9. Label smoothing 0.3 vs 0.2: no measurable difference (E013). Loss-shape knobs are flat. Hyperparameter tweaks near the current point probably give under 0.2 pp, which is inside noise.
10. Noise: runs are deterministic per seed. Seed and recipe-reshuffle noise is about ±0.2 pp on 3-seed means. Time noise is about 1% or less. Fixed costs are about 0.3-0.5 s.

Misses: I under-predicted EMA, Muon and resizing, and over-predicted E009 and E011 accuracy. My accuracy ranges centred on 0.7565 for E010 and E013 were about 0.15 pp too high, since the tip sits at 0.755. The lesson is to centre accuracy-neutral changes on the current 0.7548 value.

Unsure: how much GPU idle time or launch overhead there is under 4 CPUs. The per-step work is about 25 steps per epoch at batch 2000, so the steps are large and launch overhead is probably small, but the Muon and EMA foreach parts and the Python LR loops could matter. CUDA graphs might save 0-8%. Also unsure whether plain EMA matches Lookahead, and what the held-out seed spread is. Accuracy-neutral systems changes are the safest time wins. Any accuracy gain can be spent on epochs at about 0.18 pp per 4.8% of time.

forecasts.reason: Math is identical, so accuracy is unchanged. Compile already fuses a lot and the steps are large, so the gain is probably a few percent at most. The risk is capture failures or recompile errors across 3 resolutions, plus the larger memory use of Muon in the graph.
No measured trend for wd. The label smoothing result suggests flat sensitivity, so I centre it near zero effect. Time is unchanged.

The step probably has few host syncs, since the LR is a Python scalar written into groups and the augmentation uses boolean-mask indexing, which does sync. Removing them could give 1-4%. Accuracy is unchanged up to RNG reshuffle if augmentation changes.

Lookahead's reset of the fast weights acted as a regularizer in E005. A plain EMA with an alpha ramp likely recovers most but not all of the gain, and BN buffer averaging adds risk. I expect a loss of about 0.3 pp, which would put it under the bar.

cruxes: How much GPU idle time or host-sync stall is in the E010 step? A profiler trace would show whether CUDA graphs or sync removal can save more than 5%.
What is the true 40-seed mean accuracy of E010? A 10-seed run shows whether the 0.17 pp margin survives, and so whether epochs can be cut further.
Does a plain EMA match Lookahead? If it does, EMA could be cheaper, and the answer tells us whether the endpoint average or the weight reset gives the +1 pp.
